newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuadoran unions mobilize against austerity plan.
newsitem.headline: Ecuadoran unions mobilize against austerity plan.

text.p: Ecuadoran teachers on Saturday called a protest against the government's economic austerity measures and several unions said they will join forces to fight a steep rise in public services rates.
"We are calling all teachers, students and parents to a day of protest to be held on January 21," National Teachers Union head Stalin Vargas told Reuters after a union meeting.

The country's major labour groups decided to unite against the government's tough reforms. They will meet next weekend to discuss walking out of a social pact they entered into with President Abadala Bucaram's five-month-old administration.
The unions stopped short from calling a general strike, though labour sources said such a move could be announced next weekend.
Students have staged violent protests since the government announced a steep rise in natural gas prices on Wednesday.
Some 400 students clashed with police on Friday. Police made 54 arrests and two students and seven police were injured in stone-throwing incidents.

A total 100 people have been arrested since Wednesday, when 5,000 people, led by teachers, marched through the centre of Quito to protest against Bucaram's tough economic reforms, which include scrapping subsidies to public services rates.

Domestic gas prices shot up by 250 percent and electricity by more than 100 percent. Bus fares are doubling in price and telephone rates were also raised substantially, although authorities have not said yet by how much.
Opposition parties are considering forming a united front against the tariff rises and a planned currency cnvertibility programme that would peg the sucre to the U.S. dollar.
